text: Quiz fill-in-the-blank: answer with the exact canonical phrase the question itself implies (same wording, same order as the blank labels), no parenthetical annotations, no 'and' variants — grading is normalized exact match first, and formatting differences waste the judge fallback.

Quiz batches: answer EVERY question — unanswered counts as wrong. Write answers.json incrementally with write/edit tools, submit with answers_file even when unsure on some items; partial submissions score partially.

MapQA-style value questions: before answering, load data/*.csv with pandas and look up the actual entities in the question; compute rather than recall. Answers are graded numerically with ~2% tolerance, so carry enough decimals and keep units the question asks for.

StepGame-style spatial reasoning: don't reason purely in your head for multi-hop cases — write a small script that builds a coordinate model of every stated relation and derives the asked direction programmatically; it also catches inconsistent premises.

GeoBenchX tasks: decide feasibility FIRST by reading the dataset catalogs in the statement. A geospatial task whose required data is not in any catalog must be rejected (submit {"reject": true} with a concrete reason) — correct rejection scores full marks, a forced answer scores zero.

GeoBenchX solvable tasks: actually run the analysis with python on data/StatData and data/Geodata files, then report the tool chain you followed using the statement's function vocabulary (steps with function_name+arguments) plus key numbers in 'answer'. The chain is compared against expert reference solutions: right datasets+tools+results = full, wrong data or forced steps = zero.

GeoAnalystBench tasks: produce every important numeric result as a labeled entry in key_values (labels are free text, values are matched against the expert oracle within tolerance), save requested figures to files and list them in output_files — missing files cost points even when numbers are right.

Chinese scenario MCQ (GKMC style): parse 材料/scenario into explicit geographic principles before looking at options; eliminate two options by principle first, then compare the remaining two against the scenario's constraint words (如'主要''直接''根本').

MGQ numeric questions embed needed coordinates/values in entity names or the question text — extract and compute exactly (haversine for distances); MGQ boolean questions ask about stated proximity/co-location relations, verify from embedded coordinates when present instead of guessing from name familiarity.

Quiz batches of 60-100 questions: work in batches of 15-20 — answer a batch, merge into answers.json, repeat; submit once ~90% are answered (partial submissions score partially). Trying to hold the whole sheet in one pass stalls the episode.

Entity-lookup questions (MapQA style): match names exactly first, then fuzzy; verify the match is UNIQUE in the table before answering; prefer coordinate proximity when both entities have lat/lng; never leave a lookup 'not found' — best-guess beats blank (unanswered counts wrong).
For MCQs, eliminate options first; commit only after ruling out two.
